issues.legal_issue: A consolidation notification abates the entire pending civil proceeding concerning land brought under consolidation, including the decisions at earlier stages, rather than only the pending appeal.
material_facts: The plaintiffs’ civil suit sought a declaration of title and possession to agricultural land, and the defendants disputed rights in that land.
While the defendants’ second appeal concerning one parcel remained pending, a government notification brought the land into consolidation.
The consolidation authorities were empowered to adjudicate the competing rights, and the governing provision allowed the parties to pursue those rights before those authorities.
issues.conclusion: The second appeal concerning the parcel abated, and the civil proceeding as a whole—including the trial court and first appellate court decisions concerning that parcel—also abated, leaving the parties to pursue their rights before the consolidation authorities.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 4(1)(c) of the Bihar Consolidation of Holdings and Prevention of Fragmentation Act, 1956, read with its proviso and Section 3, a qualifying notification causes pending civil proceedings concerning rights or interests in land to abate so that consolidation authorities can adjudicate those rights without interference from civil-court proceedings. This statutory abatement differs from ordinary civil-law abatement, under which abatement of an appeal leaves the decision appealed from final. The Court relied on Ram Adhar Singh v. Ramroop Singh, Chattar Singh v. Thakur Prasad Singh, and Satyanarayan Prasad Sah v. State of Bihar.

rule.if: land_rights_civil_proceeding and land_included_in_consolidation and consolidation_notification_issued and proceeding_pending_when_notification_issued

predicates.land_rights_civil_proceeding: The parties were litigating in a civil proceeding over rights or interests in land.
predicates.land_included_in_consolidation: The land involved in the dispute was included in a consolidation process.
predicates.consolidation_notification_issued: The government issued a notification bringing the land into that consolidation process.
predicates.proceeding_pending_when_notification_iss: A proceeding concerning the land remained pending before a civil court when the notification was issued.

issues.definition: When a civil proceeding over land remains pending as the land is brought into consolidation, the proceeding and its prior decisions abate as a whole.

issues.legal_issue: Abatement of an appeal concerning one parcel does not affect a decree concerning a separate parcel when the only claimant to that separate parcel had already lost his appeal through non-substitution after death and the appellants in the later appeal claimed no interest in it.
material_facts: One defendant claimed a separate and exclusive interest in one parcel, while the defendants who later brought the second appeal claimed an interest only in another parcel.
The defendant claiming the separate parcel died while his first appeal was pending, and no legal representative was substituted for him.
Neither a legal representative nor anyone claiming through the deceased defendant brought a second appeal concerning that parcel.
The trial court had declared the plaintiffs’ title to the separate parcel, and the later appellants had no interest in it.
issues.conclusion: The deceased defendant’s appeal concerning the separate parcel had abated before the consolidation notification, leaving the trial court’s title declaration final as against him and those claiming through him. The later appellants’ second appeal and its abatement did not affect that declaration, which was restored.
issues.legal_principle: Under the ordinary civil-law concept of abatement, when an appellant dies and the necessary legal representatives are not substituted, that appellant’s appeal abates and the decision appealed from becomes final. The consolidation abatement under Section 4(1)(c) of the Bihar Consolidation of Holdings and Prevention of Fragmentation Act, 1956, affected the pending appeal of parties who claimed rights only in the other parcel; it did not unsettle the decree concerning a parcel for which no relevant appeal remained pending.

rule.if: land_title_civil_suit_and_appeal and separate_property_claim and exclusive_claimant_died_during_appeal and deceased_claimant_not_substituted and no_successor_appealed_on_property and later_appellants_lacked_interest_in_property

predicates.land_title_civil_suit_and_appeal: The dispute arose from a civil suit seeking title to land and proceeded through an appeal.
predicates.separate_property_claim: The property at issue was distinct from other property involved in the suit.
predicates.exclusive_claimant_died_during_appeal: The person appealing the decision on the property claimed a separate and exclusive interest and died while that appeal was pending.
predicates.deceased_claimant_not_substituted: No legal representative was substituted for the deceased claimant in the pending appeal.
predicates.no_successor_appealed_on_property: No legal representative or person claiming through the deceased claimant brought a later appeal concerning the property.
predicates.later_appellants_lacked_interest_in_prop: The parties whose later appeal abated claimed no interest in the property.

issues.definition: Where the sole appellant claiming a separate property dies without substitution and no successor appeals concerning it, an appeal by other parties who lack an interest in that property does not disturb the property title decree.
